scenes.headline: Why shiny objects fill Gaussian splats with floaters
scenes.sub: And how this month's papers place, clean and reason about 3D
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Nori! A splat can match one photo perfectly and be wrong from every other angle. Here's why shiny things break Gaussian splatting, and the fix.

scenes.text: A floater is a highlight stored at the wrong depth. Give the reflection its own term, and there is nothing left to fake.
scenes.say: A floater isn't noise. It's a highlight stored at the wrong depth. Give the reflection its own term, and there's nothing left to fake.

scenes.title: Two ways to paint a highlight

left.title: Splats alone
items: A bright blob hung on the fitted view's rays
Matches that view, lands wrong in every other
left.say: Splats alone hang a bright blob on the rays that saw the highlight. It matches that photo, and lands wrong from every other angle.

right.title: A separate specular term
items: The colour stays on the surface
The reflection is read along the mirror direction
right.say: The fix keeps colour on the surface and reads the reflection along the mirror direction, so it slides like a real one.

steps.say: Here's the paper's chrome toaster. The middle row is standard splatting: once the camera leaves the training poses, its reflections turn into floating streaks.
The top row gives reflections their own term, and stays close to the ground truth.

scenes.title: Mean model size, six shiny scenes
scenes.note: mean PSNR 30.40 vs 30.32 dB; the mesh is supplied
scenes.say: It's about a quarter the size at level quality on average. But the mesh is an input it was handed, not one it reconstructed.

steps.say: Next, placing objects from a single photo. Start with the photo and each object's mask.
For every pixel of an object, the model predicts which point of the object's own normalised shape it shows.
A depth model says where that same pixel sits in the room.
Every pixel is now a match. Solve the one scale, rotation and shift that fits them all, and the object lands.

scenes.text: Splats fake what they cannot model with matter. Give a reflection its own term, and the floater has nothing left to explain.
scenes.say: Splats fake what they can't model with matter. Give a reflection its own term, and the floater has nothing left to explain.

recap: A floater is a highlight at the wrong depth
A separate specular term keeps reflections in place
Per-pixel matches place objects from one photo
scenes.say: Floaters are depth errors, reflections deserve their own term, and one photo can place a room, one pixel at a time.
